test_title: PYST 13: Selection Post (Graduation Level) - GA (Held On 25 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following options is not related to the non-cooperation movement started by Mahatma Gandhi?

options.text: Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore

solution:
The correct answer is __**Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **non-cooperation movement** was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 to resist British rule in India through non-violent means.
 
• The movement included the **boycott of foreign goods**, which aimed at promoting Indian-made products and crippling British economic interests in India.
 
• The **distribution of spinning wheels** was encouraged to promote self-reliance and the use of khadi (hand-spun cloth).
 
• **Picketing at liquor shops** was part of the movement to oppose British-imposed taxes on liquor and to promote temperance.
 
• **Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore** is not related to the non-cooperation movement. It was part of a different phase in India's struggle for independence, specifically the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in 1929 where the demand for complete independence was formalized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The non-cooperation movement was a significant phase in the Indian independence struggle, involving millions of Indians who withdrew their cooperation from the British government.
 
• It was characterized by the use of non-violent methods such as non-payment of taxes, surrender of titles, and boycott of British educational institutions and law courts.
 
• The movement was eventually called off by Gandhi in 1922 following the Chauri Chaura incident, where a violent clash led to the death of police officers.
 
• The **Lahore Session** in 1929 was a turning point as it marked the formal adoption of the goal of Poorna Swaraj or complete independence from British rule.
